profiles.meeting_scenario: A brainstorming meeting in an academic ML research lab between a faculty lead and a postdoctoral researcher preparing a workshop paper follow-up to FlatNAS. Context: they want to generate concrete experiment ideas for extending FlatNAS beyond image corruption benchmarks into a stronger OOD-robust NAS story that could be pitched as a new submission in the next 6 weeks. Agenda: identify 2-3 promising extension directions, decide what kind of 'flatness-aware' search variation is worth prototyping first, and sketch a lightweight evaluation plan that can be executed with the lab's existing compute budget. Expected outcome: a short list of candidate project directions and an informal division of next steps for a pilot experiment. Both participants leave believing they have agreed on a compact first prototype, but they silently diverge on what the prototype actually includes and how its evidence will be summarized.

members.name: Dr. Lena Voronov
members.expertise: Neural architecture search, robust generalization, publication strategy
members.background: Leads a university ML research group focused on efficient AutoML and robustness; previously published on differentiable NAS and benchmark design, and tends to think in terms of paper framing, comparability to prior work, and reviewer expectations.
members.private_state: She wants a follow-up idea that is novel enough for a workshop-or-conference submission without requiring a full reimplementation of FlatNAS; she is especially concerned about telling a clean story that architecture-level flatness contributes to robustness even when trained only on in-distribution data.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing a 'small pilot', it is obvious that only the search stage should be lightweight, while final selected architectures will still get full retraining for publication-quality evidence.

If they say 'OOD robustness', the natural benchmark family is corruption robustness in the ImageNet-C/CIFAR-C tradition, because that is what FlatNAS already established and what reviewers will immediately recognize.
A result is 'stable' once the ranking of candidate architectures looks consistent across a few random seeds, even if the final report mostly highlights the best checkpoint for each selected model.
When someone says they will 'reuse the supernet', that means reusing the existing search space and weight-sharing infrastructure, not necessarily freezing the exact current training pipeline details.

members.name: Dr. Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Loss landscape analysis, SAM optimization, empirical robustness evaluation
members.background: Recently joined the lab from a group studying flat minima and optimization geometry; he is strong on efficient experimental pipelines and often interprets ideas through the lens of training dynamics and reproducibility.
members.private_state: He wants an extension that can produce convincing mechanistic evidence about why flatness-aware search helps, ideally without a massive compute bill; he is worried that a purely benchmark-driven extension will look incremental unless they can show robust behavior during search itself.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing a 'small pilot', it is obvious that both search and final evaluation should remain lightweight, so conclusions should come from supernet-derived or near-zero-cost proxies before any expensive retraining.

If they say 'OOD robustness', the most informative next step is distribution shift beyond corruptions, such as style-transfer or cross-dataset generalization, because corruption robustness is already saturated as a narrative.

A result is 'stable' only if aggregate means and variance across seeds are reported for both search outcomes and downstream retraining, since single-run best cases are not trustworthy in flatness claims.

When someone says they will 'reuse the supernet', that includes reusing the learned shared weights as part of evaluation, because the value of the extension is to avoid retraining every candidate from scratch.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a small pilot
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to start with a 'small pilot' before scaling up.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a lightweight NAS search over a reduced search space or fewer epochs, followed by standard full retraining of the top architectures for proper comparison.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the entire first study—including evaluation—should stay cheap, relying mostly on supernet-based estimates, short fine-tunes, or one-shot assessments rather than full retraining.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML brainstorming, 'small pilot' naturally sounds like shared shorthand for a resource-conscious first step, and both participants expect the exact cost profile to be obvious from their own norms.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly discuss improving 'OOD robustness' and designing a stronger OOD story.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 uses 'OOD robustness' to mean robustness to common corruption benchmarks derived from the in-distribution dataset, such as CIFAR-C, ImageNet-C, or severity-based corruption suites.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 uses 'OOD robustness' to mean broader distribution shift, especially cross-domain or style/content shifts such as CIFAR to CIFAR.1, PACS-style transfer, or synthetic style perturbations not limited to corruption taxonomies.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'OOD robustness' is standard and broad in ML research, so each assumes the other shares their preferred subcase; because both benchmark families are legitimate, neither wording sounds off.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that whatever idea they choose should yield 'stable' or 'consistent' results.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the selected architecture family should qualitatively preserve its ordering and headline claims across a handful of runs, enough to support a compelling figure and narrative.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means numerical stability must be demonstrated through explicit multi-seed averages and variance bars across the search stage and downstream evaluations before any claim about flatness can be trusted.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the language of rigor and reproducibility, but the disagreement is over the threshold for sufficient evidence rather than over whether stability matters at all, so the surface agreement feels complete.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to reuse the supernet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'reuse the supernet' to move quickly.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means they can reuse the existing FlatNAS codebase, search space, and weight-sharing training framework while still retraining extracted architectures in the usual standalone way afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means they should directly exploit the trained supernet weights or supernet-derived proxy evaluations as part of assessing candidate robustness, minimizing any from-scratch training.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In NAS discussions, 'reuse the supernet' can refer either to infrastructure reuse or to actual shared-weight evaluation, and both are common enough that the phrase passes without clarification.

turns.inner_thought: We need something that looks like a genuine FlatNAS follow-up, not a sprawling new system. Six weeks means I cannot afford a full reimplementation or an entirely new benchmark stack. A small pilot should mean we keep the search cheap—reduced epochs, maybe fewer candidate comparisons—but we still do proper standalone retraining for the selected architectures at the end, otherwise the paper will feel flimsy. If we can tell a clean story that architecture-level flatness helps robustness even from standard in-distribution training, that is a workshop paper at minimum and maybe more if the results are crisp.

I do not want us to burn compute on full retraining if the core claim can be tested from supernet-side evidence or very light follow-ups. The interesting angle is whether flatter architectures identified during search already show stronger OOD robustness in a way that hints at mechanism, ideally beyond the usual corruption-only story.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, but if we make any flatness claim, stable has to mean real seed-level evidence. I want repeated seeds at search time and in downstream evaluation, with means and variances reported, otherwise reviewers will poke holes immediately. I can say that without sounding oppositional.

turns.inner_thought: Let me narrow this so we leave with something actionable. The two directions I can imagine pitching are: first, a stronger corruption-style OOD robustness story with severity structure; second, a search-time flatness proxy that improves selection. Both should fit inside a small pilot, meaning quick search changes followed by full retraining only for a few finalists. If one direction lands, we can expand later.
